title: Coxeter presentation of a finite based root datum Weyl group
statement: Let $\mathcal R=(M,\Phi,M^\vee,\Phi^\vee,\Delta)$ be a finite reduced based root datum as defined in [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]; no group-scheme realization is assumed. Thus $M$ is a finite-rank free abelian group, $M^\vee$ its integer dual, $\Phi$ and $\Phi^\vee$ finite reduced root and coroot sets paired by $\alpha\mapsto\alpha^\vee$, and $\Delta$ is a base with the same-sign integral expansion property. For $\gamma\in\Phi$ put $s_\gamma(m)=m-\langle m,\gamma^\vee\rangle\gamma$, and let $W\subseteq\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbf Z}(M)$ be the subgroup generated by all $s_\gamma$. Then $W$ is finite and generated by $s_\alpha$ for $\alpha\in\Delta$. For distinct $\alpha,\beta\in\Delta$, let $m_{\alpha\beta}$ be the order of $s_\alpha s_\beta$ in $W$. Let $F(\Delta)$ be the group of finite words in letters $x_\alpha^{\pm1}$, with adjacent inverse letters cancelled. The homomorphism $\pi:F(\Delta)\to W$ sending $x_\alpha$ to $s_\alpha$ is surjective and its kernel is the normal subgroup generated by $$x_\alpha^2\quad(\alpha\in\Delta),\qquad (x_\alpha x_\beta)^{m_{\alpha\beta}}\quad(\alpha\ne\beta).$$ Here normal generation means all finite products of conjugates of these words and their inverses. Equivalently, $W$ is presented by these generators and relations. Roots need not span $M\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$, and when $\Phi=\Delta=\varnothing$ the group and the free group are both trivial.

source.place: Appendix C.11, printed p.610, full generators-and-relations assertion; C.19--C.20, p.611, and C.37--C.46, pp.615--618, for passage from a root datum to the real root span and faithful Weyl action. No Stacks tag states this root-system presentation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-root-datum-weyl-group] to the datum after forgetting its base. The perfect duality, finite sets, bijection and simultaneous reflection axioms are exactly those in [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. Thus $W$ is finite and its action on $\Phi$ is faithful. Put $E=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf R}(\Phi)\subset M\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf R$. Restriction $W\to\operatorname{GL}(E)$ is injective: an element in its kernel fixes every root. Its image is exactly the group generated by the restricted root reflections, so identify these groups. This also preserves the order of each product of reflections.

The given $\Delta$ is a real basis of $E$: it is a rational basis of the rational root span, and the rank of a rational matrix is unchanged over $\mathbf R$ (rank is the largest size of a nonzero minor). Give this basis the dot product $B_0$ and put $B(x,y)=\sum_{w\in W}B_0(wx,wy)$. The identity summand proves positivity; reindexing the finite sum proves $W$-invariance. For $a\in\Phi$, $s_a$ is $-1$ on $\mathbf R a$ and $1$ on $\ker(a^\vee|_E)$; invariance makes these summands orthogonal. Consequently $s_a(x)=x-2B(x,a)B(a,a)^{-1}a$, with integral coefficients on other roots. If roots $a,b$ are real proportional, any nonzero rational coordinate of $a$ shows their ratio is rational, so reducedness gives $b=\pm a$. Thus these data form a finite reduced crystallographic real root system with its prescribed base.

source.place: C.19--C.21, pp.611--612; C.29, p.614; explicit averaged form and scalar extension check.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-simple-root-reflection-generation] on this real root system. Every restricted root reflection is a word in the restricted simple reflections; injectivity of restriction makes the same identity hold on $M$. Hence the simple reflections generate $W$. They are nonidentity involutions, since $s_a(a)=-a\ne a$, and distinct simple roots have distinct reflections: equality would identify their $-1$ eigenspaces $\mathbf R a$, contrary to independence of $\Delta$. In particular the simple-reflection map is injective.

source.place: C.11, p.610, generation assertion; C.1 and C.8, pp.607,609.

proof.text: Write $P=\Phi^+$. The same-sign base condition gives $\Phi=P\sqcup(-P)$. Fix $a\in\Delta$ and $b\in P\setminus\{a\}$. Some $\Delta$-coordinate of $b$ away from $a$ is strictly positive: otherwise reducedness on $\mathbf Q a$ gives $b=a$. Subtracting $\langle b,a^\vee\rangle a$ leaves that coordinate unchanged. Since $s_a b$ is a root and has same-sign coordinates, it is positive; it cannot equal $a$, since then $b=s_a a=-a$. Applying the involution again proves $s_a(P\setminus\{a\})=P\setminus\{a\}$. These are precisely the sign-partition hypotheses needed below.

source.place: C.21, p.612, and the sign argument underlying C.10--C.11; agent expansion.

proof.text: Let $\ell(w)$ be minimal simple-word length and $a\in\Delta$. If $wa\in-P$, apply [lem-sfb-root-sign-word-deletion] to a reduced expression for $w$: it deletes one letter to express $ws_a$, so $\ell(ws_a)\le\ell(w)-1$. Conversely $w=(ws_a)s_a$ gives the reverse bound, hence equality. If $wa\in P$, set $v=ws_a$; then $va=-wa\in-P$, so the already proved implication applied to a reduced expression for $v$ gives $\ell(w)=\ell(v)-1$. Therefore $\ell(ws_a)=\ell(w)+1$. Now take any nonminimal word and its first nonminimal prefix of length $j$. Its preceding prefix $u$ is reduced of length $j-1$; the length criterion forces $u a_j\in-P$. The cited deletion lemma applied to this expression for $u$ deletes one of its letters to express $us_{a_j}$. Thus deleting that letter and position $j$ from the original word preserves its product. This proves two-letter deletion for every nonminimal word.

source.place: C.10--C.11, p.610; explicit derivation of word deletion from the cited sign-change formula, written by the worker.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-involution-deletion-presentation] with $G=W$, $I=\Delta$, and $t_a=s_a$. Finiteness supplies finite orders $m_{ab}$; steps 3 and 5 supply injectivity, nonidentity involutions, generation and two-letter deletion. Its kernel conclusion is exactly the stated normal generation by squares and pair-product words. Generation also makes $\pi$ surjective, since every simple word lifts to the identical free word. If $\Phi$ is empty then $\Delta$ is empty, the generated subgroup is $1$, and the only free word is the empty word, so the assertions hold in this case as well.

source.place: C.11, p.610, conclusion; abstract deletion characterization is the separate cited node (Bourbaki IV §1.5 Theorem 1).

The item restates C.11 for a based root datum, unchanged, keeping the empty and non-spanning cases. The route matches Humphreys 1.6–1.9 (root signs, then length and deletion, then presentation). Step 1: the finite-Weyl lemma's axioms match the definition, and faithfulness on Φ makes W→GL(span_R Φ) injective. Step 2 (elementary, checked): Δ is a real basis by the rank of a rational matrix; the averaged invariant form B makes s_a the B-reflection, since its ±1-eigenspaces are orthogonal and ⟨a,a^∨⟩=2; Q-reducedness gives R-reducedness. These are all the hypotheses of the simple-root-reflection-generation lemma. Step 3: generation, s_a≠1, and injectivity of s through the −1-eigenspaces. Step 4: the sign partition and s_a(P∖{a})=P∖{a}, which are exactly the hypotheses of the root-sign-word-deletion lemma. Step 5: the length dichotomy ℓ(ws_a)=ℓ(w)±1 from the deletion lemma, then two-letter deletion at the first non-reduced prefix; I checked the rightmost-factor convention. Step 6: every hypothesis of the new node is proved, and m_ab is finite because W is finite. New node lem-sfb-involution-deletion-presentation: statement only, self-contained, the standard deletion characterization of Coxeter systems (Bourbaki IV §1, WANTED; Humphreys 1.9).
